title: Mexico’s Olmeca Refinery Achieves Record Production in July
author: Alejandro Alegría
content:
_This article by Alejandro Alegr ia originally appeared in the [September 6,
2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/06/economia/logra-la-
refineria-olmeca-produccion-record-en-julio), Mexico's premier left-wing daily
newspaper._

The Olmeca refinery of Petróleos Mexicanos (Pemex) reached a fuel production
of **252,000 barrels per day in July** —**the highest since the plant began
operating** —which is equivalent to **a 78.75 percent increase compared with
June**.

It is the third time that these facilities, located in the municipality of
Paraíso, Tabasco, have exceeded 200,000 barrels per day. This comes six months
after they had shown a steady decline in performance.

It is also the first time the refinery has reached **74.23 percent of its
production capacity** , which is 340,000 barrels per day.

Compared with the July 2025 average of 155,000 barrels per day, fuel
production at the Dos Bocas Refinery, as it is also known, rose 62.41 percent.

In the period in question, the Olmeca Refinery contributed 21.17 percent of
Pemex's total fuel production, which amounted to 1,191,000 barrels per day. It
ranked only below the Salina Cruz Refinery, in Oaxaca, which averaged 252,000
barrels per day, and above Tula, in Hidalgo, which produced 196,000 barrels
per day.

According to data from the Ministry of Energy (Sener), demand for gasoline and
diesel so far in 2026 averages 1,300,000 barrels per day.

Although production data vary from month to month, the Olmeca refinery's
output in July was equivalent to **19.38 percent of total domestic demand**.

**Historically, Mexico has imported a little more than half of the fuel it
consumes.**

The increase in refining at these facilities is explained by the upticks in
gasoline and diesel.

In July, gasoline production averaged 108,000 barrels per day, 127.9 percent
more than in June, when Pemex reported 47,000 barrels each day. Some 87,000
barrels per day of regular fuel, or ultra-low-sulfur Magna (UBA), and 20,000
of Premium were produced.

In turn, diesel production averaged 93,000 barrels per day, a 45.78 percent
rise from the 64,000 barrels of June. All of this fuel is of the ecological
type.

The process volume—that is, the distillation of crude to separate its useful
components and turn it into final products such as fuels, plastics and other
chemicals—was 228,000 barrels per day, a 62.22 percent increase over June,
when the average was 141,000 barrels per day.

With these figures, the Olmeca Refinery reached 67.32 percent of its
processing capacity. According to Pemex, full capacity cannot be reached for
operational reasons, although it can come close to the maximum.

In July, Pemex reported a fire at the Dos Bocas Refinery, although the company
said this incident did not affect operations. Throughout the first half of the
year several incidents were also reported, although they did not affect the
facilities' activities either.
